name: Carni Shoulder Lock
summary: Carni is a leg-assisted shoulder lock in which the bottom player retains the upper arm, controls the wrist, and adjusts the hip angle without forcing the knee or shoulder.
description: Carni is a leg-assisted shoulder lock in which the bottom player retains the upper arm, controls the wrist, and adjusts the hip angle without forcing the knee or shoulder.
overview:
Carni is a leg-assisted shoulder lock in which the bottom player retains the upper arm, controls the wrist, and adjusts the hip angle without forcing the knee or shoulder.

Begin in Carni/Bottom with the opposing shoulder and upper arm controlled; this is an upper-body lock. Keep control of the triceps so the opponent cannot freely withdraw the upper arm.

Secure the wrist while keeping the shoulder and elbow within a comfortable, controlled range. Turn through the hip to support the raised knee; never pull the foot against a fixed knee. Use a small controlled adjustment through the leg-assisted arm clamp. Stop before pain or forced joint movement. Release at any tap or verbal signal. Remove wrist leverage and shoulder pressure before unwinding the leg connection.

Practice cooperatively with controlled movement. Stop at any tap, verbal signal, or distress; release all joint or neck pressure before changing direction. Do not force a trapped knee, shoulder, or neck to preserve the route.

defender.name: Carni Shoulder Lock Defender
defender.description: Recognize Carni Shoulder Lock and interrupt its required connections before the final control is established.
defender.overview:
You oppose the performer of this action. Recognize the upper-arm clamp before the wrist is fixed. Keep the elbow near the body while the shoulder connection is still forming. Clear the wrist before trying to rotate the shoulder through the enclosure. If the finish is interrupted, do not assume the Carni shoulder control has also disappeared. When the holder releases safely, restore posture in the facing closed guard.

Practice cooperatively with controlled movement. Stop at any tap, verbal signal, or distress; release all joint or neck pressure before changing direction. Do not force a trapped knee, shoulder, or neck to preserve the route.
